grades.quote: For other traps, `mtval` is set to zero, but a future standard may redefine `mtval` ’s setting for other traps.
grades.reason: Describes the machine-level mtval, not stval. It is analogous: mtval is zero for other traps and must hold valid virtual addresses. It does not state when stval holds the faulting virtual address, so it is only auxiliary.

grades.quote: for misaligned loads and stores that cause guest-page faults, a nonzero guest physical address in `htval` corresponds to the faulting portion of the access as indicated by the virtual address in `stval` .
grades.reason: Covers htval (guest physical address), not stval. It only mentions in passing that stval holds the faulting virtual address for misaligned accesses and instruction guest-page faults. That is limited, indirect help.
This is the LoongArch BADV register. The query asks specifically about RISC-V stval, so the ISA is wrong.

grades.quote: When a guest-page fault occurs in such a circumstance, the faulting virtual address written to `mtval` / `stval` is the same as would be required for a regular page fault.
grades.reason: Directly addresses stval holding the faulting virtual address for guest-page faults, including page-boundary-straddling fetches and misaligned accesses. It covers only part of the conditions and does not say when the value may be absent.
